result: Worse than the fixed strategies on 2019. Not enabled.

title: BTC weekend intraday, 5 strategies
question: Do the intraday setups make money on Bitcoin at weekends after exchange fees?
result: All 5 fail. About 0R before costs; fees cost 0.4-1.1R per trade.

title: Cost filter: skip trades where cost is more than 20% of risk
question: Does skipping small-stop trades, where costs eat the most, turn the NAS100 strategies positive?
data: NAS100 1-minute bars; first a partial period, then full 2019-2022
result: Fewer losses, still no winner. sweep_mss_fvg looked like +0.15R on the first 18 months but was -0.14R on full 2019-2022 (Lesson 2: small samples lie).

title: NAS100 intraday, 7 strategies (NY and London), full 2019-2024
question: Do the 7 written-down intraday strategies make money after costs in both periods?
data: HistData NSXUSD 1-minute bars 2019-2024; dev 2019-2022, validation 2023-2024 (splits fixed in CLAUDE.md before the run)
result: No strategy is positive in both periods; averages -0.01R to -0.37R per trade; none robust.

title: Daily trend: SMA100 long and Donchian 55/20
question: Do slow daily trend rules beat a random-timing control with the same stop and holding time?
data: HistData NSXUSD daily bars 2019-2024; dev 2019-2022, validation 2023-2024
result: Both fail: they do not beat random timing, and only 8-27 trades per period. A rising market made random entries look good (Lesson 4).

title: Measurement audit and session-validity rule
question: Are the backtest measurements sound (data holes, costs, clustered uncertainty, multiple testing)?
result: 2023 fails the session-validity rule on 119 of 256 weekdays. Conclusion unchanged: no edge after costs.

title: Real bid/ask prices, 2023
question: Does the bid-only fill model flatter the results, and what is the real spread by time of day?
data: Dukascopy USATECHIDXUSD bid and ask 1-minute bars, 2023
result: The bid-only model is not material. Spread about 1.45 pts in US hours, about 3 pts before 09:30 NY. 6 of 7 strategies at or below 0; silver_bullet +0.32R but its range crosses 0 (unproven).

title: MT5 demo spread by time of day
question: Does the broker demo feed show the same wider spread before the US open as Dukascopy?
result: 1.0 pts before the US open, 0.9 in US hours, never above 1.0. The feed looks fixed or capped, so this is weak evidence. Not Exness.

title: Real bid/ask re-test, 7 strategies, 2019-2024
question: Does any of the 7 strategies have a reliable advantage with real bid/ask prices, in both periods?
data: Dukascopy USATECHIDXUSD bid and ask 1-minute bars 2019-2024; dev 2019-2022, validation 2023-2024
result: Waiting for data. On 2026-11-19 dev coverage was 2% and validation 61%, so there is no verdict. Amendment 1 (commit 390efc1, DST clock check) was made before any strategy result.

title: Paper engine vs backtester replay
question: Does the same market data give the same signal, fill, exit and cost in the paper engine and the backtester?
result: Signals 126/126 identical; shared trades 28/28 identical. All 34 one-sided trades trace to the 0.1 minimum lot and its knock-on through the risk rules. No execution bug found.

title: Exness vs Dukascopy spread, 2023
question: Is the Exness tick file trustworthy, and how does its spread compare with Dukascopy and the 1.5-point assumption?
data: Exness USTEC ticks 2023 and Dukascopy bid/ask 2023
result: File passes all checks. Exness median 2.95 pts before the US open (similar to Dukascopy) and 2.93 in US hours (about double Dukascopy's 1.45). The 1.5 assumption is understated.

title: Exness spread by year, 2019-2024
question: Is the Exness spread similar in every year, and are the yearly files usable?
data: Exness USTEC ticks 2019-2024, checked against HistData NSXUSD
result: Usable: 2021, 2022, 2023 (median 2.75-2.94 pts). Not usable: 2019 and 2020 (too few complete days), 2024 (price gap to HistData 17.29 pts). Exness cannot cover both test periods.
